display.purpose: Numbers and identity: brand mark, page titles, KPI values, kiosk clock.

title.purpose: Serif uppercase panel/section headers, in amber-bright.

body.purpose: Table cells, form copy, running text.

label.purpose: Uppercase micro-labels: field labels, table headers, tags, KPI labels.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one call-to-action fill in the system: amber background, dark text, bold uppercase-leaning label.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { all: unset; cursor: pointer; background: #c68a2e; color: #1c1815; font-weight: 700; padding: 9px 16px; border-radius: 3px; font-size: 12.5px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.5px; text-align: center; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #e0a949; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #e0a949; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: default; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Transparent, bordered — used for lower-emphasis actions like Cancel or Sair.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { all: unset; cursor: pointer; background: transparent; border: 1px solid #413a2f; color: #c9c0af; padding: 9px 16px; border-radius: 3px; font-size: 12.5px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.5px; text-align: center; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: #c68a2e; color: #e0a949; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Reserved for destructive row-level actions — outline by default, fills solid on hover as a deliberate friction point.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { all: unset; cursor: pointer; background: transparent; border: 1px solid #a13d2b; color: #e5806c; padding: 5px 9px; border-radius: 3px; font-size: 11px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.5px; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: #a13d2b; color: #f4efe6; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Char background field with a hairline border; focus is a color-only state change, no glow.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; } .ds-label { font-size: 10.5px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.6px; color: #c9c0af; } .ds-input { background: #1c1815; border: 1px solid #413a2f; color: #f4efe6; padding: 8px 9px; border-radius: 3px; font-size: 13px; font-family: inherit; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #c68a2e; }

components.name: KPI Card
components.description: The signature dashboard tile — a left accent border in amber (or ember-red for warning metrics) is the one deliberate side-border accent in the system.
components.css: .ds-kpi { background: #252019; border: 1px solid #413a2f; border-left: 3px solid #c68a2e; border-radius: 3px; padding: 14px 16px; } .ds-kpi-label { font-size: 10.5px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 1px; color: #c9c0af; } .ds-kpi-value { font-family: Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif; font-size: 24px; color: #f4efe6; margin-top: 4px; }

components.name: Panel
components.description: A bordered content container with an amber-bright uppercase serif header rule — used for tables, forms, and grouped content.
components.css: .ds-panel { background: #252019; border: 1px solid #413a2f; border-radius: 3px; padding: 18px 20px; } .ds-panel-title { font-family: Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif; font-size: 14px; color: #e0a949; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.8px; margin: 0 0 14px; border-bottom: 1px solid #413a2f; padding-bottom: 8px; }

components.name: Status Tag
components.description: Full-pill status marker: a saturated text color on its own muted, near-black tint of the same hue. Ok/warn/bad are the only three states.
components.html: Faturado Pendente Cancelado
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-block; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 20px; font-size: 10.5px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.4px; } .ds-tag-ok { background: #28351f; color: #8fbd6f; } .ds-tag-warn { background: #3a2b13; color: #e0a949; } .ds-tag-bad { background: #3a1c15; color: #e5806c; }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Link
components.description: Default/hover/active states for the main sidebar — active uses the Smoke surface and bold amber-bright text.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { text-decoration: none; cursor: pointer; padding: 9px 10px; border-radius: 3px; color: #c9c0af; font-size: 13px; display: block; } .ds-nav-link:hover { background: #2f2921; color: #f4efe6; } .ds-nav-link-active { background: #3c352b; color: #e0a949; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Kiosk Register Button
components.description: Signature oversized touch-target CTA from the tablet kiosk sub-world — same amber fill as the primary button, but scaled for a thumb, not a mouse, with the kiosk's larger 8px radius.
components.css: .ds-qk-register { all: unset; cursor: pointer; background: #c68a2e; color: #1c1815; font-weight: 700; font-size: 20px; padding: 22px 54px; border-radius: 8px; letter-spacing: 1px; text-align: center; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-qk-register:hover { background: #e0a949; }

narrative.overview:
Sistema 364 is the shift lead's board on the wall of a working kitchen: dark, no-nonsense, built to be scanned at a glance while hands are busy with something else. It exists to track lots, costs, shifts, and stock across four brands sharing one back office — precision under pressure, not persuasion. Every screen defaults to dense, tabular, low-glare: charcoal surfaces, paper-colored text, and a single warm amber signal for what needs a hand on it right now.

The palette is deliberately narrow — a handful of char/smoke tones, one paper text color, one recurring accent — so that amber reading as "active, primary, or worth noticing" never has to compete with decorative color elsewhere. The system rejects light backgrounds, drop shadows, and rounded-corner softness as its default register; those belong only to the one sub-world built for a different physical context (the ponto kiosk touchscreen).
keyCharacteristics: Dark charcoal ground with a single warm amber signal, not a multi-color palette.
Georgia serif reserved for numbers and headings; everything operational reads in a plain UI sans-serif.
Uppercase, letter-spaced micro-labels used relentlessly as the connective tissue between data points.
Flat by default — depth comes from tone steps and hairline borders, never shadows.
Sharp 3px corners on desktop/office screens; a distinct, larger-radius, big-touch-target language on the tablet kiosk.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Amber is the only accent color allowed to mean "primary, active, or pay attention." Every other color in the system is either structural neutral (char/smoke/paper) or a narrow functional state (danger/success). Don't introduce a second decorative accent color.

rules.name: The Serif-For-Numbers Rule
rules.body: Georgia appears only on headings, brand marks, and numeric/identity display values — never on body copy, labels, or table cells. If it's data being scanned in bulk, it's sans-serif; if it's a headline number or a name, it's serif.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never cast a shadow, at rest or on hover. A card sits "above" the page only because it's a lighter tone step with a border, not because it's lifted.

dos: Do keep amber as the only color that means "primary, active, or attention" — its frequent reuse across nav/buttons/KPIs/focus is the system's signature, not a bug to fix.
Do pair every dark surface step with a 1px border rather than a shadow to signal a boundary.
Do use the uppercase, letter-spaced Label style for anything that annotates data (field labels, table headers, KPI labels, tag text) rather than inventing a new caption style.
Do use Georgia only for numbers, headings, and identity marks — never for body copy or labels.
Do give the kiosk shell its own larger radius and touch-target scale rather than reusing office-shell 3px controls at tablet size.
donts: Don't add box-shadow anywhere in the office or kiosk shell — depth is tone-step + border only.
Don't introduce a second decorative accent color alongside amber; new semantic states should draw from the existing danger/success pairs (ember-red/coral-alert, field-green) before adding a new hue.

Don't carry the kiosk's larger radius (8-10px) or oversized touch targets into the office shell, or the office shell's 3px sharpness into the kiosk — they're deliberately different form languages for different physical contexts.
Don't mix the print ficha's black-on-white paper world with the dark office/kiosk token set; it's an intentionally separate visual register for a printed artifact.
